summary: The bill authorizes $5 million per year in grants to states for stillbirth surveillance, data collection on risk factors, and public health capacity building, while directing HHS to issue standardized data collection guidelines to states and develop public educational materials on stillbirths.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $6 million annually in new federal appropriations ($5M for surveillance grants and $1M for guidelines/education) for fiscal years 2026-2030. This directly expands government spending on public health activities, though the amounts are modest relative to the federal budget.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.

The bill amends the Public Health Service Act to fund stillbirth surveillance, data collection, and educational guidelines through HHS and state health departments. This increases federal public-sector involvement in maternal health data and awareness, which aligns modestly with public health approaches rather than purely market-based care.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, border policy, or immigrant protections.
The bill focuses exclusively on stillbirth data and education; it does not address abortion access, restrictions, or related policies.
No provisions concern military or defense spending.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill develops educational awareness materials on stillbirths but does not involve schools, school funding, or education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
By authorizing new appropriations without offsetting cuts, the bill implicitly accepts additional deficit spending, though the scale is very small.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related policies.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
The bill requires de-identified data collection consistent with existing privacy laws but introduces no new tech or privacy regulations.
No provisions address labor unions, worker protections, or employment policy.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
